I use iPhone Mirroring every day to quickly access my iPhone on my Mac, and this year the feature is getting even better. Apple has just released the public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate, which bring three major updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything new.

macOS 27: What's new with iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window using any app that supports iOS 27. Right now, that only includes Apple's first-party iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, resize support will expand rapidly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: Smaller, Actual Size, and Larger. What changed in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

There are several other updates to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Access Control Center
  • DRM video support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring did not allow access to Control Center. In macOS 27, you can access Control Center with the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or via the Display menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected videos on your Mac through iPhone Mirroring. Previously, all DRM-protected videos would only display a black screen when iPhone Mirroring was active.

macOS 27 also introduces a new app icon design for iPhone Mirroring, keeping it consistent with the style of several other Apple built-in apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried the public beta? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.
